## Historical audit: S0069

**Scope:** Chunk 1 of 3 only. Source: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_probes/C1/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. All citations below refer to this file. Neither reference nor rendered pixels are visible in the supplied observations.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal | The student was asked to reconstruct one indoor photograph as editable, separate SceneAct meshes, matching viewpoint, placement and materials; diagnostic probes were prohibited (student request, line 1). The student’s kitchen-showroom interpretation and image anchors are estimates, not independently verified scene facts (student response, line 3). |
| Initial build | Code specifies multiple assets: architectural shell, two timber posts, cabinetry, ovens, island, sink, hob, hood and kettle. It specifies colors, grain strips, a hood noise bump, camera and lights. Named children group parts, but sink and hob remain separate from the island; names and intended support comments do not establish physical contact or complete composite movement (student response, line 6). |
| Audit input and adoption | A **source-audit-only user/controller prompt**, not an identified teacher diagnosis, requested checks on dimensions, keys, World initialization, grouping and local materials before execution (line 4). The next student program added validation helpers, explicit hood-parent assertions and World fallback; its code was subsequently executed (lines 6–7). No separate teacher message, detection or diagnosis is visible. |
| Validation | Step 1 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and Blender file, and was selected (execution result, line 8; select, line 9). This establishes a successful run, not visual fidelity, accurate pose, material appearance, contacts or editability under later operations. |
| Autonomous revision | After receiving the step-1 render and a comparison request (line 10), the student reported a too-small kitchen, overly central timber and occluding foreground surfaces. It **hypothesized**, rather than proved, that camera placement outside the shell caused framing disagreement. It changed camera position, target and lens, moved and narrowed the foreground post, extended the shell and adjusted support heights while preserving main object dimensions and lighting (student response, line 12; execute, line 13). These visual claims cannot be independently checked here. |
| Second run | Step 2 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and scene, and was selected (execution result, line 14; select, line 15). The visible record contains no independent geometric or visual assessment of the revision. |

**Outcome and lessons.** The observed outcome is two technically successful renders and a provisional step-2 selection; overall correctness and final outcome are **unknown**, not a demonstrated formal success or algorithm failure. There is no empty patch or technical interruption in this visible portion. A transferable distinction is that a source audit and successful render can check execution while leaving framing, physical connections and semantic completeness unverified. The camera-outside-shell explanation and improvement from the coupled camera, shell and post changes remain task-specific hypotheses; unseen chunks may contain further evidence, but are not inferred here.
